key_insight: A PICNN can serve as the prediction step in a physics-preserving two-phase porous-media solver, then be corrected to enforce thermodynamic consistency, mass conservation, and bounded solutions.
engineering_relevance: This offers a mesh-local, flux-based ML surrogate that is better suited than standard PINNs for porous-media flow with discontinuous permeability and interfacial flux continuity.
method: Train a physics-informed CNN on finite-volume residuals rather than pointwise PDE residuals.
Compute interfacial fluxes with TPFA using neighboring cell-centered values to approximate normal gradients.
Apply a post-processing correction to restore energy stability, mass conservation, and bounds preservation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results showing that the finite-volume-residual PICNN can replace the traditional prediction solver within the physics-preserving framework and outperform standard PINN-style locality handling.
watch_item: The approach depends on a carefully designed correction step and FV/TPFA discretization, so implementation quality and compatibility with complex geometries or strongly heterogeneous media may affect robustness.
paper_title: The PICNN-Assisted Physics-Preserving Scheme for Thermodynamically Consistent Two-Phase Flow in Porous Media
